newsitem.title: USA: Rubin - cigarette tax hike could deter tobacco use.
newsitem.headline: Rubin - cigarette tax hike could deter tobacco use.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Tuesday that tobacco use could be deterred by the cigarette tax increase contained in the balanced budget deal reached Monday by the White House and Congress.
"We have an increase in cigarette tax which could deter (tobacco) use, which also promotes health," Rubin told the Cable News Network while praising the overall budget deal.
The pact calls for a balanced federal budget for the first time in a generation and cuts taxes by $90 billion over the next five years. It raises the $0.24-per-pack cigarette tax by $0.15.
Rubin was asked by CNN if the cigarette tax increase would directly benefit the administration's sought-after children's health program.

"It will be sufficient to more than cover the addition in the children's health care benefits over the original budget agreement," he said. "The cigarette tax has fully funded the increase over the budget agreement in children's health care."
